title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Civil Affairs on Issuing the Measures for the Pension and Compensation for Judicial Police of the People's Courts and People's Procuratorates
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Civil Affairs

Notice on Issuing the Measures for Pension and Preferential Treatment of Judicial Police of People's Courts and People's Procuratorates

Fa Fa [1998] No. 6

To the High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, and Civil Affairs Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government:

We hereby issue the Measures for Pension and Preferential Treatment of Judicial Police of People's Courts and People's Procuratorates to you for implementation.

May 14, 1998

Measures for Pension and Preferential Treatment of Judicial Police of People's Courts and People's Procuratorates

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Measures are formulated in accordance with the People's Police Law of the People's Republic of China, relevant national laws, regulations, and policies on pension and preferential treatment, and with reference to the Measures for Pension and Preferential Treatment of People's Police of Public Security Organs, for the purpose of properly handling pension and preferential treatment for casualties among judicial police of People's Courts and People's Procuratorates.

Article 2 Civil affairs organs at all levels shall fully perform their functions as government departments, diligently fulfill their duties, strictly implement existing laws, regulations, and policies on pension and preferential treatment, and accurately and promptly handle matters concerning pension and preferential treatment for casualties among judicial police in accordance with the nature of judicial police work.

Article 3 The political work departments of People's Courts and People's Procuratorates at all levels shall be responsible for the specific work concerning pension and preferential treatment for casualties among judicial police.

Article 4 The political work departments of People's Courts and People's Procuratorates at all levels shall properly handle the reception of visitors and policy propaganda related to pension and preferential treatment for casualties. They shall care for the work and life of injured or deceased judicial police and their family members, and, in accordance with relevant state provisions, do their utmost to help them resolve difficulties and problems.

Article 5 The political work departments of People's Courts and People's Procuratorates at all levels shall strictly manage the relevant materials of injured or deceased judicial police, maintain detailed records, and establish archives classified by sacrifice, death on duty, and death from illness, with one file per person, for long-term preservation.

Chapter II Death Pension

Article 6 The death of a judicial police officer of a People's Court or People's Procuratorate shall be categorized based on the nature of death as:

(1) Revolutionary martyr;
(2) Death on duty;
(3) Death from illness.

Article 7 A judicial police officer who dies shall be approved as a revolutionary martyr if meeting any of the following conditions:

(1) Killed or retaliated against by a criminal suspect, defendant, or criminal due to the performance of trial or procuratorial duties;
(2) Died a heroic death while investigating criminal activities, suppressing ongoing crimes, pursuing, arresting, or guarding criminal suspects, defendants, or criminals, quelling riots or disturbances, or urgently handling major public security incidents;
(3) Died from a recurrence of the wound within one year after being injured in the acts described in subparagraph (2), or after the injury resulted in disability and the disability was assessed and certified, and the certificate was issued;
(4) Killed or retaliated against by a criminal due to maintaining public order;
(5) Died while protecting or rescuing the lives of people, state and collective property, or the lawful property of other citizens;
(6) Killed or retaliated against by a criminal due to correctly implementing the Party's line, principles, and policies, and safeguarding the interests of the state and the people;
(7) The circumstances of the death are particularly outstanding, sufficient to serve as a model for future generations.

Article 8 Approval procedures for revolutionary martyrs:

(1) The People's Court or People's Procuratorate at or above the county level where the deceased was employed shall ascertain the circumstances of the death, provide relevant supporting materials, and, after soliciting opinions from the civil affairs organ at the same level and the competent department of the superior People's Court or People's Procuratorate, submit a report to the people's government of the county (city, district) where the deceased was located; the civil affairs organ, as a functional department of the government, shall carefully review the submitted materials, and if necessary, may, with the cooperation of the People's Court or People's Procuratorate, verify the circumstances of the death.
(2) The people's government of the county (city, district), upon determination that the conditions for revolutionary martyr are met, shall report level by level to the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government. After the civil affairs department (bureau) provides preliminary review opinions, the provincial, autonomous regional, or municipal people's government shall approve. The People's Court or People's Procuratorate of the county (city, district) shall promptly copy the martyr approval materials submitted by the local county (city, district) people's government to the provincial, autonomous regional, or municipal people's government to the political work department of the High People's Court or People's Procuratorate of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.
(3) For circumstances of death that are particularly outstanding, the Ministry of Civil Affairs shall approve.
(4) For special or complicated circumstances of death, civil affairs organs, People's Courts, or People's Procuratorates at all levels shall closely cooperate to jointly conduct investigation, evidence collection, review, and conclusion. If the conditions for revolutionary martyr are not met, the civil affairs organ shall promptly notify the deceased's employer.

Article 9 A judicial police officer who dies shall be approved as having died on duty if meeting any of the following conditions:

(1) Died due to an accident not attributable to their own fault or unavoidable while on duty or while traveling to or from work;
(2) Died from a recurrence of a wound more than one year after the assessment and certification of disability resulting from combat;
(3) Died from a recurrence of a wound after the assessment and certification of disability resulting from duty;
(4) Died from an occupational disease (with reference to the Measures for the Scope of Occupational Diseases and the Handling of Patients with Occupational Diseases revised and issued by the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Labor and Personnel, Ministry of Finance, and All-China Federation of Trade Unions);
(5) Died suddenly from illness while executing a task.

Death resulting from a medical accident shall also be treated as death on duty.

Article 10 Death on duty of a judicial police officer shall be examined and approved by the People's Court or People's Procuratorate at or above the county level where the deceased was employed, and shall be reviewed and supervised by the civil affairs organ that pays the one-time pension.

Article 11 The nature of death of a judicial police officer who dies from illness shall be determined by the People's Court or People's Procuratorate at or above the county level where the deceased was employed.

Death by suicide resulting from contradictions among the people, or death due to an accident while not performing duties, shall be treated as death from illness.

Article 12 For the death of a judicial police officer, based on the nature of death and the deceased's salary at the time of death, the civil affairs organ at the place of household registration of the deceased's family, as certified by the certificate, shall calculate and pay a one-time pension. The standard for the one-time pension is:

(1) Revolutionary martyr: 40 months' salary;
(2) Judicial police officer who died on duty: 20 months' salary;
(3) Judicial police officer who died from illness: 10 months' salary.

Article 13 For a judicial police officer who has rendered meritorious service or received honorary titles (including posthumous citation or recognition of merits) and dies, the one-time pension shall be increased by the following percentages:

(1) Awarded the honorary title of Hero Model by the state: an increase of 35%;
(2) Awarded the honorary title of Hero Model by the Supreme People's Court or the Supreme People's Procuratorate: an increase of 30%;
(3) Awarded a first-class merit: an increase of 25%;
(4) Awarded a second-class merit: an increase of 15%;
(5) Awarded a third-class merit: an increase of 5%.

Article 14 If a judicial police officer who has died is approved as a revolutionary martyr and meets any of the following conditions, their family may receive a regular pension:

(1) The father, mother, foster parent, husband, or wife has no work capacity and no source of income, or although having a certain amount of income, it is insufficient to maintain the local general standard of living;
(2) Children under the age of 18, or over 18 but without a source of income due to schooling or disability;
(3) Younger siblings under the age of 18 who were solely supported by the deceased during their lifetime.

Article 15 If the family members of a revolutionary martyr are solitary elders or orphans, the regular pension shall be increased, with the increase percentage generally not less than 20% of the regular pension they are entitled to.

When the recipient of a regular pension moves their household registration, the transfer procedures for the regular pension shall be handled simultaneously. The civil affairs organ at the place of household registration move-out shall be responsible for paying the regular pension for the current year. The civil affairs organ at the place of household registration move-in shall, based on the transfer procedures, pay the regular pension starting from January of the following year at the standard prescribed by the local authority.

If a person receiving a regular pension dies, the regular pension shall cease, and an additional half-year's regular pension shall be paid as a funeral subsidy.

Article 16 If a judicial police officer dies on duty or from illness and meets the conditions set forth in the Interim Provisions on Subsidies for the Living Difficulties of Survivors of Deceased State Organs and Institutional Staff issued by the Ministry of Personnel and the Ministry of Finance, the employer shall pay a living allowance to their survivors.

Article 17 If a judicial police officer who has made special contributions in police work dies, a one-time special pension may be paid in addition to the pensions stipulated above.

Article 18 The Certificate of Revolutionary Martyr, the Certificate of People's Police Who Died on Duty, and the Certificate of People's Police Who Died from Illness shall be uniformly printed by the Ministry of Civil Affairs. The management of the certificates shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

Chapter III Disability Pension

Article 19 Disability of judicial police of People's Courts and People's Procuratorates shall be categorized based on the nature of the disability as:

(1) Disability due to combat;
(2) Disability due to duty.

Article 20 A judicial police officer who is disabled by a criminal while suppressing or investigating criminal activities, arresting, pursuing, or guarding criminal suspects, defendants, or criminals, quelling riots or disturbances, or urgently handling major public security incidents shall be deemed to have a disability due to combat.

Article 21 The specific scope of disability due to duty for judicial police officers includes:

(1) Disability resulting from an accident not attributable to their own fault or unavoidable while undergoing training, performing duty, or traveling to or from work;
(2) Disability incurred while maintaining public order, rescuing or protecting the lives of people, state and collective property, or the lawful property of other citizens;
(3) Disability due to an occupational disease.

Disability resulting from a medical accident shall also be treated as disability due to duty.

Article 22 The grade of disability shall be determined based on the degree of loss of work capacity and impact on daily living ability. The grades of disability due to combat or duty are: Special Grade, First Grade, Second Grade Class A, Second Grade Class B, Third Grade Class A, and Third Grade Class B. The specific conditions for determining disability grades shall be implemented in accordance with the Conditions for Assessing the Disability Grades of Revolutionary Disabled Servicemen.

Article 23 The medical assessment of the disability condition of a disabled judicial police officer shall be conducted by a disability medical assessment team designated by the civil affairs organ at or above the county level after the completion of medical treatment; the medical assessment of disability due to occupational diseases shall be conducted by an occupational disease assessment department designated by the provincial civil affairs organ.

Article 24 Procedures for assessing and approving disability:

(1) The individual shall submit a written application to their employer, explaining the circumstances of the disability and the condition of the injury; after review, the applicant's employer shall prepare supporting materials, together with the individual's disability file materials (including original evidence, medical records, and materials provided by on-site witnesses, etc.), the written application, and recent half-length bareheaded photographs (wearing uniform) of the individual, and submit them to the civil affairs organ at or above the county level for review.
(2) If, after review, the civil affairs organ deems the applicant eligible for disability assessment, it shall notify the individual to go to the designated disability medical assessment team for a disability assessment. Based on the assessment, the civil affairs organ shall prepare a comprehensive report, fill in the Form for Approval of Disability Grade and the disability certificate, and, together with the application and the employer's supporting materials, submit them level by level to the superior civil affairs organ for approval.
(3) If, after review, the civil affairs department (bureau) of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government deems the applicant eligible for disability assessment, it shall sign the approval opinion on the Form for Approval of Disability Grade, affix its seal, complete the disability certificate, affix an embossed seal, and send the disability certificate through the county-level civil affairs organ to the applicant's employer, which shall be responsible for handing it over to the applicant.
If the conditions for disability assessment are not met, the civil affairs organ shall state the reasons on the Form for Approval of Disability Grade, affix its seal, and return it together with other submitted materials to the civil affairs organ at the applicant's place of household registration.
The applicant's employer shall report the disability assessment status to the superior People's Court or People's Procuratorate and the political work department of the High People's Court or People's Procuratorate of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for the record.

Article 25 For disability due to combat or duty, if an application for disability assessment is filed within three years after the completion of medical treatment, with file records and conclusive evidence, and the condition meets Third Grade Class B or above, a disability grade may be assessed; if an application for supplementary disability assessment is filed more than three years after the completion of medical treatment, with file records or conclusive evidence, and the condition meets Second Grade Class B or above, supplementary disability assessment procedures may be handled.

Article 26 If the original disability grade no longer matches the current disability condition due to changes in the condition, the disability grade shall be adjusted in accordance with the provisions.

Article 27 Issuance and management of disability certificates:

(1) Disabled judicial police officers due to combat or duty, after having their disability grade assessed by the civil affairs department (bureau) of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, shall be issued the Certificate of Disability Pension for People's Police uniformly printed by the Ministry of Civil Affairs.
(2) The Certificate of Disability Pension for People's Police is a valid certificate for a disabled judicial police officer to prove their disability grade and to enjoy pension benefits. It shall be properly kept and shall not be altered, lent, or transferred without authorization.
(3) If the disability certificate is damaged due to improper safekeeping, the party concerned shall promptly report to the issuing county-level civil affairs organ. After review, if the county-level civil affairs organ deems the certificate unusable, it shall fill in the Form for Reporting Replacement or Additional Issuance of Disability Certificate for Disabled Persons and a new disability certificate, and, together with the party's application and the damaged old certificate, submit them level by level to the civil affairs department (bureau) of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for replacement.
(4) If the disability certificate is lost, the party concerned shall make every effort to find it and promptly report to the issuing county-level civil affairs organ. If it cannot be found within six months, after the party publishes a declaration of loss, the county-level civil affairs organ shall fill in the Form for Reporting Replacement or Additional Issuance of Disability Certificate for Disabled Persons and a new disability certificate, and, together with the party's application, submit them level by level to the civil affairs department (bureau) of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government. After approval, a new number shall be assigned and a new certificate shall be issued.

Article 28 Pension for disabled judicial police officers:

(1) A disabled judicial police officer shall be entitled to a disability health allowance from the date of approval of the disability assessment and shall enjoy relevant work-related injury and pension benefits.
(2) Retired or retired disabled judicial police officers of Special Grade or First Grade who are unable to care for themselves and genuinely require assistance with daily living and dietary activities may receive a nursing fee.
The standard for nursing fees shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Ministry of Civil Affairs and the Ministry of Finance, and shall be paid by the employer responsible for paying salary or retirement benefits.
(3) During hospitalization for recurrence of a wound, the meal expenses of a disabled judicial police officer, and travel, accommodation, and meal expenses for treatment in another location or for fitting a prosthetic limb due to wound recurrence, shall be handled by the employer in accordance with work-related injury benefits.
If auxiliary devices are needed due to the injury, the specific provisions of the Ministry of Civil Affairs or the local authority shall apply.

Article 29 Upon the death of a disabled judicial police officer, in accordance with relevant provisions, the disability health allowance and nursing fee shall cease, and the certificate shall be canceled. Their family members may enjoy the following benefits:

(1) If death occurs within one year after the completion of medical treatment and the issuance of the disability assessment certificate due to recurrence of a wound resulting from disability due to combat, the civil affairs organ shall, in accordance with the pension provisions for revolutionary martyrs, pay a one-time pension to the family members. If the family members meet the conditions for receiving a regular pension, they may receive a regular pension in accordance with the provisions and enjoy the treatment of family members of revolutionary martyrs.
(2) If death occurs more than one year after the completion of medical treatment and the issuance of the disability assessment certificate due to recurrence of a wound resulting from disability due to combat, or if death occurs after the completion of medical treatment and the issuance of the disability assessment certificate due to recurrence of a wound resulting from disability due to duty, the civil affairs organ shall, in accordance with the standard for death on duty, pay a one-time pension to the family members. The employer shall pay a living allowance to the survivors in accordance with the provisions.
(3) If a disabled judicial police officer dies from illness, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the provisions for death from illness of the employer. The civil affairs organ shall pay a one-time pension to the family members in accordance with the provisions for death from illness, and the employer shall pay a living allowance to the survivors in accordance with the provisions.

Article 30 When the disability pension relationship is transferred, the disability health allowance for the current year shall be paid by the civil affairs organ at the place of move-out, and from January of the following year, it shall be paid by the civil affairs organ at the place of move-in.

Article 31 If a disabled judicial police officer falls under any of the following circumstances, the civil affairs organ at or above the county level shall cancel their disability certificate, cease the pension, and report to the civil affairs department (bureau) of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for the record:

(1) Death;
(2) Settlement abroad;
(3) During a period of imprisonment, deprivation of political rights, or being wanted.

Article 32 For a disabled judicial police officer whose criminal circumstances are particularly serious, the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government may cancel their disability pension.

Chapter IV Supplementary Provisions

Article 33 The death and disability pension and preferential treatment for judicial police of specialized People's Courts and People's Procuratorates shall be implemented in accordance with these Measures.

Article 34 The preferential treatment for injured or deceased judicial police officers and their family members shall be determined by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government based on local actual conditions.

Article 35 These Measures shall be interpreted by the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

Article 36 These Measures shall take effect as of the date of issuance.
